title: I created a Free Chaotic 2D Multiplayer Physics-Based Browser Brawler using AI
author: fjorgemota
selftext:
I created a game called Vibe Fighter, and I used many AI tools to help develop it: 

\- Claude Sonnet (the preferred model for UI/text/frontend development)  
\- Claude Opus (very good at creating videos/audios)  
\- DeepSeek 4.1 Flash (not so good with images, but pretty good with backend/bot development)  
\- Ornith 1.5 35B A3B (I used it more before I got OpenCode Go to use DeepSeek 4.1 Flash.. it is pretty good for a local model, IMHO)  
\- Qwen Image 2.1 (which created the weapons images).

  
Right now, I have two AI subscriptions: Claude Pro and OpenCode Go. In my experiments, I found that DeepSeek is pretty good at code development, but it is not so good at creating texts/translations/UI. I prefer to use Claude Sonnet for anything involving texts and UI development. And Claude Opus for creating videos (like the one above, or the trailer of the game that you can see at my profile) and songs (it created it using web audio API).

  
The game was fully developed using TypeScript (the backend/server also uses TypeScript), and even with all these tools it took about \~2 months of development, in special working on improving the whole gameplay experience, adding weapons, maps, and the other features that make the game fun. The whole game has a ton of tooling that helps AI to perform better, like the whole reproduction system - that allows the AI to "play" the game and see what's happening there - about \~4k thousand tests, and a strong focus on reusability (adding a map or weapon is stupid simple, for instance)

You can play it for free at [https://vibefighter.io/](https://vibefighter.io/) \- directly at the browser, with no downloads required.

PS for the mods: Given the game is free to play I used the "Demo |  Project | Workflow". There is a store on the game, but it is fully optional. I can change to "Commercial Self Promotion" if needed.

comments.author: thebuddybud
comments.body: This is just a bad copy of stickman fight on steam..

comments.author: Delicious_Stress_911
comments.body: it looks (and obviously is) worse than "stickfighters: the game" and you didn't even mention it as inspiration. all in all a pinnacle human accomplishment.

replies.author: fjorgemota
replies.body:
Hey! Yes. Stick Fight is an inspiration, in special the ragdoll physics chaos. I did add many things that I didn't show on the video that do not exist at all the main source of inspiration, though, like the authoritative physics simulation (stick fight doesn't do that by any means..), chaos director (with both spectators participation as well as ghost votes, where dead players also vote), bots (which are adaptive to the human skills), many different weapons and maps, and so on.

All in all, I'd say that yes, stick fight is an inspiration, but no, vibe fighter isn't a copy of it.
